coolant_dry.name: Dry Cutting
coolant_dry.description: No coolant - relies on air cooling and proper speeds
coolant_dry.science: Heat concentrates at cutting edge. Must reduce speed to prevent thermal damage to tool coating. Effective for cast iron and some aluminum operations.

coolant_flood.name: Flood Coolant
coolant_flood.description: Standard flood coolant - baseline cooling and chip evacuation
coolant_flood.science: Removes heat from cutting zone, lubricates, and flushes chips. Industry standard baseline performance.

coolant_mist.name: Mist Coolant
coolant_mist.description: Atomized coolant - good chip evacuation, moderate cooling
coolant_mist.science: Evaporative cooling effect with lubrication. Less thermal shock than flood. Good for graphite and when flood isn't feasible.

coolant_air.name: Air Blast
coolant_air.description: Compressed air only - chip evacuation priority
coolant_air.science: Convective cooling clears chips effectively. Works well with coated carbide at appropriate speeds. Ideal for aluminum HSM.

coolant_tsc.name: Through-Spindle Coolant
coolant_tsc.description: High-pressure coolant through tool - optimal cooling
coolant_tsc.science: Direct delivery to cutting edge maximizes heat removal. Hydraulic chip breaking. Essential for difficult materials and deep features.

coolant_mql.name: MQL (Minimum Quantity)
coolant_mql.science: Reduces friction coefficient by 40-60%. Near-dry with excellent surface finish. Best for aluminum and brass finishing.

hsm_mode.name: High-Speed Machining
hsm_mode.description: Light cuts at high speeds with advanced look-ahead
hsm_mode.science: Uses 50-100+ block look-ahead for constant chip load in complex geometry. Requires reduced engagement but allows much higher surface speeds.
hsm_mode.howToCheck: HSM is a machining strategy, not a specific option. Check if your control has: look-ahead (Setting 59 on Haas, G05.1 on Fanuc, CYCLE32 on Siemens). If it can process programs smoothly at high feeds, you can use HSM strategies.

fanuc_aicc.name: AI Contour Control (AICC)
fanuc_aicc.science: Advanced acceleration/deceleration control analyzes upcoming path. Reduces cycle time 10-25% while maintaining accuracy. G05.1 Q1 to activate.
fanuc_aicc.howToCheck: MDI mode: Type G05.1 Q1 and press Cycle Start. If no alarm, AICC is available. Check Parameter 1604 bit 0 (AIA) = 1. Option code: AICC-I or AICC-II.

fanuc_nano.name: Nano Smoothing
fanuc_nano.description: Fanuc Nano interpolation for mirror-finish surfaces
fanuc_nano.science: Sub-micron path smoothing with 1000+ block look-ahead. Creates seamless transitions between G01 segments. Essential for die/mold finishing.
fanuc_nano.howToCheck: Check Parameter 8486 (NANO SMOOTHING). System screen → Parameter → Search 8486. If parameter exists, feature available. Option: Nano Smoothing.

fanuc_hpcc.name: High-Precision Contour (HPCC)
fanuc_hpcc.description: Fanuc high-precision mode for tight tolerances
fanuc_hpcc.science: Combines smooth TCP control with servo tuning optimization. Reduces following error by 50%. Ideal for 5-axis simultaneous work.
fanuc_hpcc.howToCheck: MDI: Type G05 P10000 and press Cycle Start. If PS alarm 5323 appears, HPCC not available. Check System → Options → 'HIGH PREC CONT CTRL'.

heidenhain_cycle32.name: CYCLE 32 Tolerance
heidenhain_cycle32.science: Defines path tolerance for geometry optimization. Control smooths path within tolerance band. Lower values = more accurate but slower.
heidenhain_cycle32.howToCheck: In program, try adding CYCLE32(0.01). If alarm 1123 appears, option not installed. Check MOD Functions → Machine Options → 'HSC package'.

heidenhain_adp.name: ADP (Advanced Dynamic Prediction)
heidenhain_adp.science: Analyzes geometry ahead and pre-calculates optimal axis dynamics. Reduces jerky motion on complex 3D surfaces by 40%.
heidenhain_adp.howToCheck: Check if M120 is listed in machine's M-code table. MOD → Machine Functions → Active M-functions. Option: Dynamic Precision package.

heidenhain_hsc.name: HSC Mode (M120-M128)
heidenhain_hsc.science: M120 activates HSC with automatic jerk limiting. Different M-codes optimize for roughing vs finishing. Up to 30% faster cycle times.
heidenhain_hsc.howToCheck: Test M120 in MDI mode. If machine accepts without alarm, HSC is available. Check MOD → Options → 'High Speed Cutting' must show YES.

heidenhain_afc.name: AFC (Adaptive Feed Control)
heidenhain_afc.description: Heidenhain adaptive feed based on spindle load
heidenhain_afc.science: Monitors spindle power and automatically adjusts feed rate. Prevents tool breakage in hard spots, speeds up in soft areas. 10-40% faster cycles.
heidenhain_afc.howToCheck: Go to MOD → Machine Options. Look for 'Adaptive Feed Control' (option 45). Try FUNCTION AFC CTRL in program - alarm means not installed.

siemens_cycle832.name: CYCLE832 Top Surface
siemens_cycle832.description: Siemens high-speed settings for surface finish
siemens_cycle832.science: Activates compressor, look-ahead optimization, and jerk limiting in one cycle. Parameters control tolerance vs speed tradeoff.
siemens_cycle832.howToCheck: Try CYCLE832(0.01) in a test program. PS alarm 14009 means not installed. Check HMI → Diagnostics → System → Software options → 'Top Surface'.

siemens_compcad.name: COMPCAD Compressor
siemens_compcad.science: Compresses G01 linear segments into smooth spline curves. Reduces program size 60-80% and improves surface quality.
siemens_compcad.howToCheck: In MDI type COMPCAD and press Cycle Start. Alarm 14009 means option not available. Check Option data bit MD18360 $MN_MM_SPLINE_MODE.

siemens_dynfinish.name: DYNFINISH Mode
siemens_dynfinish.science: Optimizes servo response for minimal following error during finishing passes. Reduces path deviation at corners.
siemens_dynfinish.howToCheck: Test DYNFINISH in program. Check MD32400 $MA_AX_JERK_MODE for supported dynamic modes. Option: 'Advanced Surface Motion'.

siemens_traori.name: TRAORI 5-Axis Transform
siemens_traori.science: Activates kinematic transformation with tool center point control. Essential for 5-axis simultaneous with RTCP.
siemens_traori.howToCheck: Check Diagnostics → NC/PLC → Options → 'Transformation package'. Try TRAORI in MDI - alarm means 5-axis package not installed.

siemens_soft.name: SOFT Mode
siemens_soft.science: Limits jerk for smoother motion and reduced machine vibration. Best for finishing and 5-axis work. Opposite of BRISK.
siemens_soft.howToCheck: SOFT/BRISK are standard commands. Test SOFT in MDI mode. Check MD32402 $MA_MC_DYNAMIC_MODEL for tuning.

okuma_supernurbs.name: Super-NURBS
okuma_supernurbs.science: Processes spline curves natively instead of linear approximations. Eliminates faceting, reduces cycle time 15-30%, improves finish 40%.
okuma_supernurbs.howToCheck: Check OSP screen: Setup → Optional Functions → look for 'Super-NURBS'. Try G05.1 Q1 in MDI - alarm 1037 means not installed.

okuma_navi_lg.name: Machining Navi L-g
okuma_navi_lg.science: AI system learns optimal parameters from sensor data. Suggests speeds/feeds and detects chatter. Reduces trial-and-error setup.
okuma_navi_lg.howToCheck: Press Operation on OSP panel. Look for 'Machining Navi' icon/button. If not present, option not installed. Check System → Spec Confirm.

okuma_hypersurface.name: Hyper-Surface
okuma_hypersurface.science: Advanced algorithm for die/mold finishing. Combines Super-NURBS with adaptive acceleration for glass-like surfaces.
okuma_hypersurface.howToCheck: Try G05.1 Q3 in MDI mode. Check Setup → Optional Functions → 'Hyper-Surface'. Also visible in System → Spec Confirm screen.

okuma_5axis_tuning.name: 5-Axis Auto Tuning
okuma_5axis_tuning.science: Automatically calibrates rotary axis dynamics. Compensates for thermal growth and mechanical variation. Run after warmup.
okuma_5axis_tuning.howToCheck: Go to Setup → 5-Axis Functions. If '5-Axis Auto Tuning' option appears, it's installed. Also check Spec Confirm for '5-axis package'.

okuma_collision.name: Collision Avoidance System
okuma_collision.science: Continuously monitors tool/workpiece/fixture for potential collisions. Stops machine before crash. Essential for complex 5-axis setups.
okuma_collision.howToCheck: Look for 'CAS' indicator on main OSP screen (usually top right). Setup → CAS Settings. Check Spec Confirm for 'CAS' option.

mazak_smoothai.name: Smooth Ai
mazak_smoothai.science: Machine learning optimizes acceleration/deceleration based on geometry. Learns from each program run. Up to 30% faster cycles.
mazak_smoothai.howToCheck: Press Menu → Settings → Options. Look for 'SmoothAi' or 'Ai Technology'. On SmoothX controls, check System Config → Installed Options.

mazak_vac.name: Variable Acceleration Control
mazak_vac.description: Mazak adaptive acceleration for complex geometry
mazak_vac.science: Adjusts axis acceleration based on upcoming path complexity. Smoother motion on 3D surfaces while maintaining speed on simple moves.
mazak_vac.howToCheck: Standard on SmoothX/SmoothG controls. Check diagnosis screen for 'VAC' status. Older controls: Setup → NC Options list.

mazak_scc.name: Smooth Corner Control
mazak_scc.science: Automatically detects corners and optimizes deceleration/acceleration. Prevents overshoot and maintains accuracy.
mazak_scc.howToCheck: Standard on Smooth controls. Check Settings → Machining Cond. → 'Corner Control' section. Can adjust tolerance band.

mazak_avc.name: Active Vibration Control
mazak_avc.science: Monitors spindle vibration and adjusts speed/feed in real-time. Eliminates chatter marks without operator intervention.
mazak_avc.howToCheck: Look for G10.9 support in G-code list. Settings → Machining Cond. → 'Vibration Control'. Option on newer Smooth controls only.

mazak_intelligent_pocket.name: Intelligent Pocket Milling
mazak_intelligent_pocket.science: Automatically generates efficient pocket paths with constant tool engagement. Reduces cycle time 20-40% vs conventional pocketing.
mazak_intelligent_pocket.howToCheck: Test G12.1 in MDI mode. If alarm, pocket milling cycles not installed. Check Diagnosis → NC Option → 'Pocket Milling'.

haas_g187.name: G187 Smoothness
haas_g187.science: E parameter sets tolerance (0.001-0.250"). Lower E = tighter tolerance. P sets minimum corner feed percentage.
haas_g187.howToCheck: G187 is standard on all Haas mills. Test: G187 P1 E0.01 in MDI. P1=rough, P2=medium, P3=finish. No alarms means working.

haas_lookahead.name: Look-Ahead (80 Block)
haas_lookahead.science: Pre-processes 80 blocks to optimize acceleration. Best combined with G187 for HSM toolpaths. Enable with Setting 59.
haas_lookahead.howToCheck: Standard on NGC controls. Check Setting 59 (Look-Ahead) should be ON. Press SETTINGS, page to 59. Set to ON for HSM.

haas_g154.name: G154 Work Offsets
haas_g154.science: 99 additional work offsets beyond G54-G59. Essential for pallet systems and multi-part fixtures. G154 P1 = offset 1 of 99.
haas_g154.howToCheck: Standard on all Haas machines. Try G154 P1 in MDI. If alarm, firmware may need update. Works with any Haas control.

haas_rigid_tap.name: Rigid Tapping
haas_rigid_tap.science: Spindle encoder synchronizes with Z-axis for backlash-free tapping. No tension/compression holder needed. Setting 133 controls peck retract.
haas_rigid_tap.howToCheck: Standard on all Haas. Test with M29 (engage rigid tap) then G84. If spindle has encoder, it will work. Check Parameter 57.

haas_wips.name: WIPS Probing
haas_wips.science: Automated part and tool measurement cycles. G65 P9xxx calls standard probing macros. Reduces setup time 50-80%.
haas_wips.howToCheck: Press LIST PROGRAM, look for O09xxx probing programs. If not present, WIPS not installed. Check Setting 59 (Probe Type) > 0.

haas_m143.name: M143 Part Ready
haas_m143.science: Sends signal to external device when part is complete. Useful for automation and part counting systems.
haas_m143.howToCheck: Standard M-code. Test M143 in MDI. Check Parameter 57 bit 24 for M143 output configuration.

makino_sgi.name: SGI.5 Super Geometric Intelligence
makino_sgi.science: 5th generation geometric intelligence. Analyzes 2000+ blocks, optimizes feed for surface quality. Industry-leading die/mold finish.
makino_sgi.howToCheck: Try G05 P2 in MDI mode. Check Pro6 control: Menu → System → Options → 'SGI' or 'Super GI'. Also in machine spec sheet under software options.

makino_gi.name: GI Geometric Intelligence
makino_gi.science: Intelligent feed control based on curvature analysis. Automatically slows for tight radii, accelerates on straights.
makino_gi.howToCheck: Standard on most Makino machines. Test G05 P1 in MDI. P0 turns off, P1 = standard GI, P2 = SGI (if equipped).

makino_igs.name: Inertia Active Control
makino_igs.description: Makino servo tuning for heavy tables
makino_igs.science: Adapts servo response based on table/workpiece mass. Maintains accuracy with heavy fixtures. Auto-calibrates during warmup.
makino_igs.howToCheck: Check Pro6: Menu → System → Machine Config → 'Inertia Control'. Option on larger machines (a81/a92). Run calibration cycle.

hurco_ultimotion.name: UltiMotion
hurco_ultimotion.science: Proprietary motion algorithm with 10,000+ block look-ahead. Constant velocity cornering with minimal jerk. Up to 30% faster than standard.
hurco_ultimotion.howToCheck: Standard on all Hurco mills with WinMax. Check WinMax: Settings → Machine Config → 'UltiMotion' enabled. Green indicator when active.

hurco_swept.name: Swept Surface Mode
hurco_swept.science: Optimizes toolpath execution for complex swept surfaces. Reduces cutter marks and improves blend between passes.
hurco_swept.howToCheck: In WinMax conversational: Surface tab → look for 'Swept Surface' option. Also in NC mode via G-code header settings.

hurco_afc.name: Adaptive Feed Control
hurco_afc.science: Monitors spindle load and automatically adjusts feed rate. Prevents tool breakage, optimizes metal removal rate.
hurco_afc.howToCheck: Check WinMax: Run Mode → Options → 'Adaptive Feed Control'. If greyed out, option not installed. Requires spindle load sensor.

mitsubishi_sss.name: SSS Control (Super Smooth Surface)
mitsubishi_sss.science: Combines high-speed processing with servo optimization. Reduces machining striations by 60%. Popular for automotive dies.
mitsubishi_sss.howToCheck: Check M800/M80 control: Setup → System Options → 'SSS Control'. Test G05.1 Q1 in MDI. Alarm 3065 means not installed.

mitsubishi_omr.name: OMR-DD (Optimal Machine Response)
mitsubishi_omr.science: Calibrates servo response for minimal following error. Essential for high-speed die/mold with DD spindles.
mitsubishi_omr.howToCheck: Test G08 P1 in MDI mode. Check Parameters 1281-1284 for OMR settings. Option on M800/M80 series with DD motors.

brother_rapidarc.name: 3D Rapid-Arc
brother_rapidarc.science: Optimized arc interpolation for tapping and small hole work. Reduces tap-to-tap time by 40% with rigid tapping.
brother_rapidarc.howToCheck: Standard on Speedio series. Check C00 control: Parameters → System → 'Rapid Arc'. Test G05 P1 at high feeds.

brother_overlap.name: Hi-Speed Overlap
brother_overlap.science: Overlaps Z retract with XY move and tool change. 0.9 second chip-to-chip. Critical for high-mix production.
brother_overlap.howToCheck: Standard on Speedio. Test M228 in MDI. Check Parameters → ATC → 'Overlap Mode'. Should show 'Enabled'.

kitamura_arumatik.name: Arumatik-Mi Control
kitamura_arumatik.science: Fast processing CNC with icon-based programming. Combines look-ahead with thermal compensation for micron-level accuracy.
kitamura_arumatik.howToCheck: Check Arumatik screen: Settings → Options → 'Motion Control Package'. Green indicator = active. All MyCenter machines included.

sodick_linear.name: Linear Motor HSM
sodick_linear.science: Zero-backlash linear motors with 100m/min rapids. No mechanical wear. Micro-precision positioning for graphite electrodes.
sodick_linear.howToCheck: All Sodick HSM machines have linear motors by default. Check machine spec plate for 'Linear Motor Drive'. Not an option - standard equipment.

sodick_lnmotion.name: LN Motion Control
sodick_lnmotion.science: Optimized for graphite and copper electrode machining. Sub-micron positioning with vibration damping.
sodick_lnmotion.howToCheck: Check LN controller: Menu → System → Options → 'LN Motion'. Standard on most Sodick HSM models.

roders_rms.name: RMS6 High-Speed Control
roders_rms.science: Purpose-built for 42,000+ RPM machining. 200μs block processing. Designed for micro-milling and graphite.
roders_rms.howToCheck: RMS6 is standard Röders control. No option check needed - if it's a Röders, you have it. Check software version in System Info.

fidia_hifi.name: Hi-Fi Look-Ahead
fidia_hifi.science: Massive look-ahead buffer for large aerospace parts. Optimizes 5-axis motion for composite trimming and large die work.
fidia_hifi.howToCheck: Check Fidia control: Setup → Options → 'Hi-Fi Path Processing'. All modern Fidia controls include this. Also verify in System Info screen.

dmg_mpc.name: MPC (Machine Protection Control)
dmg_mpc.science: Real-time monitoring prevents crashes and overloads. Automatically reduces feed during hard spots. Protects investment.
dmg_mpc.howToCheck: On CELOS screen, look for 'MPC' app icon. Settings → Technology Cycles → 'MPC' should show 'Active'. Check with DMG dealer for activation.

dmg_atc.name: ATC (Adaptive Technology Cycle)
dmg_atc.science: Learns from each cutting operation. Automatically adjusts parameters based on measured forces and power consumption.
